newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA AXE HARRY FOR ENGLAND TEST.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-AUSTRALIA AXE HARRY FOR ENGLAND TEST.

text.p: Australia, mauled by a rampant New Zealand forward pack at the weekend, reacted on Monday by dropping prop Richard Harry for Saturday's one-off rugby union test against England.
The Wallabies were overpowered by the All Black forwards during a 30-13 defeat in Christchurch on Saturday, prompting coach Greg Smith to axe Harry in one of four changes to a 24-man squad.
Centre Daniel Herbert was also omitted to make way for the return of Jason Little, who missed the Bledisloe Cup loss because of a hip injury.
Australia enjoyed a further boost ahead of the encounter against England at the Sydney Football Stadium with the return of full-back Matt Burke.
Burke, a key attacking player and the Wallabies' goal-kicker, has been sidelined for several weeks with a groin injury and appears certain to replace Stephen Larkham in the starting line-up.
In the forwards, Harry was replaced by uncapped New South Wales front row teammate Cameron Blades, whose brother Andrew was already in the squad.
Smith also called up number eight Michael Brial and fly-half Elton Flatley while leaving out flanker Toutai Kefu. Neither Brial or Flatley are expected to make the starting line-up.
Smith was forced to modify his midfield options after centre Pat Howard was ruled out with a fractured right ankle and ligament damage.
Howard, who sustained the injury when he fell awkwardly in a tackle at Lancaster Park, was scheduled to undergo surgery on Monday and was expected to be out of action for up to 10 weeks.

Forwards - Andrew Blades, Cameron Blades, Michael Brial, Marco Caputo, Matt Cockbain, Troy Coker, John Eales (captain), Michael Foley, Daniel Manu, Ewen McKenzie, Garrick Morgan, Brett Robinson, David Wilson.
Backs - Matthew Burke, Elton Flatley, George Gregan, Mitch Hardy, Tim Horan, James Holbeck, Stephen Larkham, Jason Little, Sam Payne, Joe Roff, Ben Tune.
